sections.h2: Which way should I sell a Gastonia house?
sections.html:
Gastonia owners can hire an agent, look for a buyer unaided, or take a cash offer on the house unrepaired. Repairs, timing and the discount you will accept for speed decide it.

  • Agent: widest exposure, with prep work, showings and a fee.
  • Unaided: no fee, but the contract work is yours.
  • Cash: your schedule and no repair list, usually at a lower number.

Many Gastonia houses date from the mill era, so cash offers often come up for homes carrying deferred work.

sections.h2: What is the story behind Gastonia, and what did it leave behind?
sections.html:
Gastonia began in 1873 as a small railroad depot and incorporated in 1877, according to the city's history page. Two railroad lines crossing, plus the steam-powered textile mill, drove the early growth.

The city started with roughly 200 residents on under one square mile. It was voted county seat in 1911 and has run under a council-manager government since 1919. The page calls Gastonia the largest of Gaston County's 15 municipalities, with more than 72,000 residents and about 51.99 square miles.

That mill history left a mix of housing ages. Houses built around the textile era tend to have older wiring, plumbing and foundations, which is worth an inspection when you set the asking figure.

sections.h2: How does Gaston County value a Gastonia house?
sections.html:
The Gaston County tax office values every parcel, and the commissioners voted in 2025 to adopt a four-year reappraisal cycle. State law requires one at least every eight years, so Gaston now reappraises twice as often.

A county news release says the proposed Schedule of Values was first presented on August 25, that an updated version was posted on September 29, and that adoption was scheduled for the October 27 commissioners meeting. Ask the Gaston County Tax Office whether it was adopted and what your new assessed value is, because that outcome should come from the office itself.

The county FAQ gives the formula: tax value divided by 100, times the rate. The county and the cities publish a revenue-neutral rate in the budget cycle, and a higher value may or may not mean a higher bill.

sections.h2: What are the Gaston County tax dates?
sections.html:
Bills are due September 1, and interest starts January 6 under G.S. 105-360. The county's tax collection page repeats that schedule.

sections.h2: Who records a Gastonia sale, and where is the courthouse?
sections.html:
Deeds go to the Gaston County register of deeds, and the closing attorney normally handles the filing and the fees on your settlement statement. Ask for that statement in writing before the closing date.

The city's history page tells how the county seat moved here. A 1906 referendum moved it from Dallas to Gastonia, and the first courthouse here opened with a commissioners meeting on January 2, 1911. The current courthouse opened June 15, 1998 at North Marietta Street and Long Avenue. The older building on South Street was restored and dedicated in 2002 as the James B. Garland Municipal Business Center.

Court filings tied to a sale, such as an estate matter, go to the courthouse, so plan a trip or ask your attorney to file for you.

sections.h2: Can a Gastonia owner who is 65 or disabled get a lower tax bill?
sections.html:
Possibly. The state allows one of three relief programs, filed with the county assessor on Form AV-9, and the elderly or disabled exclusion removes half the appraised value or $25,000, whichever is greater. The state form prints the 2026 income limit as $38,800.

A disabled veteran exclusion is a separate program. Ask the Gaston County assessor which one fits and what deadline applies to your parcel.

sections.h2: What if I inherited a Gastonia house?
sections.html: A small estate can be collected by affidavit instead of full administration, with a $20,000 personal property limit for an intestate estate under G.S. 28A-25-1. A house is real property, so ask an estate attorney or the county court clerk who may sign the deed before you accept any offer.

sections.h2: What should a Gastonia seller prepare before listing?
sections.html:
Gastonia sellers do best when they sort out three things before the first showing: the age of the major systems, the paperwork on the lot, and who has authority to sign. Houses from the textile era are often sound but carry old wiring, plumbing and foundations, so an early inspection tells you what a buyer will find.

  • Hire an inspector, or at least a roofer and an electrician, to price the big items.
  • Pull the parcel record from Gaston County and check the square footage and bedroom count.
  • Find the deed, any survey and payoff statements for each loan or lien.
  • For an inherited house, confirm with the clerk or an attorney who can sign.

The county's reappraisal visits every property and compares similar sales, so a house with improvements that are not on record may be valued low, while one with errors in its listing may be valued high. If something looks wrong on your record, raise it with the tax office before it becomes a bill.

If the house is vacant, secure it and keep the grass cut, since neglected properties draw complaints. Buyers paying cash will often accept such a house unrepaired, which is why owners with a vacant mill-district house often compare that route with a repair-and-list plan.

sections.h2: How long does a Gastonia sale take?
sections.html:
Ask each buyer for a closing date in writing, since the route drives the calendar. A listing runs through showings, an offer, an inspection period and the buyer's loan, and a repair request can restart talks. Cash deals can close sooner since nobody is waiting on a lender's appraisal.

Gastonia is the biggest of Gaston County's 15 municipalities, so many buyers and sellers come through the same courthouse and register of deeds. Your attorney handles the search for liens, the closing and the recording, and can tell you how soon the deed will be filed after funds clear.

sections.h2: What questions should a Gastonia seller put to a buyer?
sections.html:
Put the same questions to every buyer and keep the answers in writing. That makes two offers easy to compare, even when one looks larger.

  • Is the price firm, and what could change it after an inspection?
  • Does the buyer need a loan, or is it a cash purchase with proof of funds?
  • Who pays for the title search, the attorney and the recording?
  • How many days will the buyer take to close?
  • Will the buyer take the house with the furniture and debris still in it?

Cash Home Buyers gives written answers on Gastonia houses, including inherited homes, rentals and vacant properties.

sections.h2: How do I read Gastonia's old county seat history when I sell?
sections.html:
The courthouse story matters mostly as context for where paperwork goes. Gaston County business moved from Dallas to Gastonia after a 1906 referendum, and today the register of deeds, the clerk's office and the tax office serve owners from the Gastonia area, so one trip often covers several steps.

If you are selling an inherited or tax-delinquent house, line up the clerk's file, the tax balance and the deed history together. Having all three in hand before an offer arrives keeps a Gastonia closing from stalling over a missing document.

faqs.q: Is Gastonia the Gaston County seat?
faqs.a: Yes, since a vote in 1911, according to the city's history page.

faqs.q: How often does Gaston County reappraise?
faqs.a: Every four years, a cycle the commissioners adopted in 2025.

faqs.q: Where is a Gastonia deed filed?
faqs.a: With the Gaston County register of deeds, usually by the closing attorney.

faqs.q: I inherited a house in Gastonia. Can I sell it?
faqs.a: Yes, once you hold legal authority to sign. G.S. 28A-25-1 describes a small estate affidavit, and the court clerk can say which route fits.
